da662c89ea6eee7c: KLANG, Oct 25 — The Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, has said that his views, criticisms and concerns on matters relating to the state administration are not intended to interfere in the affairs of the state government.
Instead, His Royal Highness said such matters were raised to ensure that the welfare and well-being of the people remained a top priority.

“I do not want the people to view my criticisms as a dispute or conflict between me and the government. Instead, I want every criticism to be seen as part of my responsibility to ensure that the state administration always looks after the interests of the people and the future of Selangor.

“However, what saddens me is that the criticisms or ‘titah’ (royal pronouncements), as they are referred to in royal parlance, have been misinterpreted by certain quarters and a handful of politicians, as though I intend to interfere in the affairs of the state government or practise absolute monarchy,” Sultan Sharafuddin said.

Sultan Sharafuddin said this at the ceremony for the proclamation of titles, oath-taking and pledging of allegiance by the Orang-Orang Besar Istana and Dato’ Diraja Selangor, as well as the conferment of Selangor state honours, in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee of His Royal Highness’s reign, held at the Balairung Seri of Istana Alam Shah here today.

Sultan Sharafuddin also stressed that he was fully conversant with the provisions of the law and understood the extent of his role and responsibilities under the system of constitutional monarchy and parliamentary democracy practised in the country and Selangor.
His Royal Highness also respects the provisions of the Selangor State Constitution 1959 and the relevant provisions of the Federal Constitution concerning his position and powers as Sultan.

“All this while, I have discharged my duties as ruler in accordance with the trust and responsibilities vested in me, and I believe that every party entrusted with responsibilities in the government has its respective duties, which must be respected and carried out with full integrity.

“To my government, I urge you to work hard to achieve success and progress in all fields. I want to see Selangor continue to develop as a progressive and competitive state with a high level of modernisation and a knowledgeable, accomplished population, while continuing to uphold religious values, good manners and humanity,” His Royal Highness said.
Sultan Sharafuddin said the measure of a state’s progress should not be based solely on billions of ringgit in investment, rapid development or high gross domestic product figures.

His Royal Highness said it was pointless for a state to possess great wealth if its people continued to struggle, as true progress meant ensuring that the benefits of the state’s wealth could be enjoyed by all its people.
“For example, in a developed and wealthy state, the people, especially the poor and underprivileged, should be able to benefit from and enjoy that wealth.

“The people should always be supported through access to quality education, affordable housing, ample employment opportunities, and a clean and healthy environment. What is important to emphasise is that the people must feel that they have not been forgotten by the government in its pursuit of rapid development,” Sultan Sharafuddin said.
Sultan Sharafuddin also described his reign, which began in 2001 as the Sultan of Selangor, following 33 years as the state’s Raja Muda, as a journey that had been far from short.

The Sultan said that throughout this period, His Royal Highness and the people of Selangor had faced various challenges and trials, while also witnessing rapid development and changes in the state. These experiences had taught him much and deepened his understanding of the true meaning of a ruler’s responsibilities.
During his reign, four Menteri Besar had served alongside Sultan Sharafuddin to lead the state government.

“In my view, being a Sultan is not a position or status to be proud of. Rather, it is a trust and responsibility bestowed by Allah to safeguard the well-being and prosperity of all the people living in Selangor, while preserving the sanctity and dignity of Islam.

“I still remember the oath I took during my installation and coronation ceremony as Sultan on March 8, 2003, in which I pledged to uphold the sanctity of Islam at all times and govern Selangor with fairness, impartiality and honesty for the well-being of the people, in accordance with the Selangor State Constitution 1959.

“I take this opportunity to reiterate and renew my pledge to continue upholding the sanctity of Islam and to govern with fairness, honesty and responsibility for the prosperity of the people and my beloved state of Selangor,” His Royal Highness said.

Sultan Sharafuddin also pledged to continue to fulfil his responsibility to uphold Islam as the religion of the state and ensure that it continued to be respected and practised by Muslims in Selangor without being questioned.

At the same time, His Royal Highness urged the people of Selangor to continue living in peace and respecting and understanding one another, given the state’s multiracial, multireligious and diverse population. Differences in race, religion and culture should not become reasons for hostility.

The Sultan also urged the people to exercise caution when discussing sensitive issues and not to misuse freedom of speech in ways that could offend the race, religion or beliefs of others, while continuing to respect one another.

“Freedom must be accompanied by responsibility. Differences of opinion must be accompanied by courtesy, and progress must go hand in hand with human values. I want Selangor to remain a peaceful and prosperous state where its people live in unity,” Sultan Sharafuddin said.

His Royal Highness also expressed gratitude to Allah for granting him the opportunity to fulfil this trust during his 25 years as Sultan. He thanked all the people of Selangor for their unwavering support, prayers for him and his family, and the confidence they had placed in him to rule the state throughout this period.

“I do not regard these 25 years as a personal achievement. Instead, I see them as a trust and a service to the people that I must fulfil. As long as Allah grants me the strength and opportunity, I will continue to discharge this trust to the best of my ability.

“I pledge to continue looking after the people, safeguarding the religion and protecting Selangor from any threats. May Allah continue to protect Selangor, grant well-being to all its people, and bless the state with lasting peace, prosperity and success,” Sultan Sharafuddin said. — Bernama

324e3ae89e5b34b5: KUALA LUMPUR: Lawyer Kamal Hisham Jaafar, who represents the two policemen in the assault case involving Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain, said there was no need for others to bring up his past.
"My role is on a professional basis and not on a personal basis," he said in a statement.
Regarding questions about his past, Kamal, a former legal counsel for the Johor royal family, said he was grateful to the Sultan, who had granted him an unconditional pardon.
"So, the matter should not be touched on or questioned by any party to preserve the dignity and grandeur of His Majesty, and it is also considered settled," he said.
Claims about Kamal relate to legal battles linked to his stint as a legal counsel, which have circulated on social media.
He said he was now carrying out his duties as a defence lawyer and solicitor as usual.
"I have never been convicted of any criminal offence, as falsely alleged on social media.
"If there were any criminal conviction, the Malaysian Bar would certainly not have issued my practising certificate," he said.
Kamal said he was handling the case pro bono, as he had done with many others.
He added that his legal team was collecting evidence of condemnation, insults, slander and criticism that crossed the line of the law, with a view to taking appropriate action.

On Wednesday, Shuhaily, who is the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general, pleaded not guilty to two charges of voluntarily causing hurt to two Special Branch policemen last month.
Kamal represents the two policemen, Lance Corporals Muhammad Ekmal Sofwan Driman, 25, and Mohamad Faiz Saman, 40.
eea1957117724a6f: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 25 — The Penang Island City Council (MBPP) has ordered an immediate halt to condominium construction and roadworks on a hillside near the site of a landslide that claimed a man’s life in Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong, here today.
MBPP mayor Datuk A. Rajendran said the stop-work order was issued to facilitate further investigations into the incident.
“The road and condominium projects have been ongoing for more than a year, while slope stabilisation works are also being carried out in the area.
“So far, we have recommended that the occupants of six houses identified as potentially unsafe relocate temporarily to prevent any untoward incidents,” he told reporters at the scene today.
In the incident, which occurred at about 8.36am, Wong Kar Lin, 73, a doctor, was found trapped after a landslide struck his house. Rescuers recovered his body at about 11.20am.
The victim’s wife, Chang Mei Nuo, 68, and his mother-in-law, Wong Poh Lim, in her 80s, managed to escape shortly after the incident.

Meanwhile, State Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said slope stabilisation works were being carried out in the area, but some sections had yet to be completed when the landslide occurred.
He said the immediate priority was to ensure the safety of nearby residents while allowing the relevant authorities to investigate the cause of the incident.

“Unfortunately, the section that had yet to be completed was the one affected by the landslide. Further investigations are ongoing before more detailed information can be provided,” he said. — Bernama
d0babfb5210ec5e9: PHILLIP ISLAND: Marc Marquez was denied the chance Sunday to stretch his world championship lead over injured Jorge Martin with the last Australian MotoGP at Phillip Island cancelled due to treacherous conditions.
Organisers pulled the plug despite a sell-out crowd with persistent rain and poor visibility making racing unsafe.
The Moto3 and Moto2 races were also called off.
"Limited visibility has resulted in the cancellation of the Australian MotoGP," organisers said.

It was an inglorious end to nearly three decades of the sport at the waterfront circuit two hours from Melbourne, with the Australian race moving to a city-centre street circuit at Adelaide next year.

While a blow for Ducati's Marquez, it was an escape for Aprilia's Martin, who had been ruled out of the race with a fractured forearm sustained when he crashed during the sprint on Saturday, won by his fellow Spaniard.
He risked sliding further behind seven-time world champion Marquez with only four legs of the season to go, starting next week in Malaysia.
Instead he will leave Australia just 10 points adrift.
Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi is third in the standings, 50 points behind Marquez.
Whether Martin can ride at Sepang remains to be seen.
His team said in a statement the break was not as bad as initially thought and he would not need to return home to Spain for surgery.
"The only confirmed injury is a non-displaced fracture of the distal radius," Aprilia said, meaning the bone remains aligned.
"Consequently the rider will not be returning to Spain and will undergo the necessary treatment over the coming days."
The picturesque and often windswept Phillip Island track has been a staple on the calendar since 1997.
But its contract expires this year.
Promoter MotoGP Sports Entertainment wanted to broaden its appeal and shift it to Melbourne's Albert Park, which hosts the Australian Formula One.
The Victoria state government was adamant it should remain at Phillip Island.
With negotiations breaking down, South Australia stepped in and secured the race for six years from 2027 in Adelaide – the first MotoGP to be held in a city centre location. - AFP
022dbd12f1f43e9b: GEORGE TOWN: An environmental group has demanded an explanation from the Penang government over a fatal landslide in Paya Terubong, questioning whether sufficient safety measures were in place.

Sahabat Alam Malaysia president Meenakshi Raman said the death of a doctor in this morning's incident was a devastating reminder of the dangers posed by extensive hill-cutting in environmentally sensitive areas.

She said residents and non-governmental organisations had repeatedly warned about the risks of major works in the area, which is prone to landslides and is also the site of a road project involving extensive hill-cutting.
"Unfortunately, we have been proven right once again," she said in a statement.
Meenakshi claimed photographs of the affected area showed bare, unprotected slopes, raising questions over monitoring and mitigation measures.
She demanded that the state government explain how the tragedy happened and why it could not have been prevented.
"Was there any monitoring of the slopes? Why were there insufficient mitigation measures?" she asked.
Meenakshi also criticised the authorities over what she described as a failure to learn from previous incidents, warning that inadequate oversight could have deadly consequences.
She called on the state government to take action if negligence was established and ensure those responsible were held accountable.
She said immediate slope rehabilitation and additional preventive measures were also needed to protect nearby residents and prevent further loss of life and property.
The landslide at Taman Seri Rambai this morning claimed the life of 73-year-old doctor Wong Kar Lin.
A stop-work order has been issued, while occupants of five houses have been advised to evacuate as a precaution.
Penang Island City Council (MBPP) mayor Datuk A. Rajendran said the affected project involved the construction of a road and apartments and had been ongoing for more than a year.
47c677c90a7be2b1: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's Islamic finance industry is evolving beyond traditional banking to play a wider role in people's lives and the economy, from helping microentrepreneurs build sustainable businesses to enabling small and medium enterprises (SMEs) to enter global markets.
Over more than four decades, the industry has grown from a niche segment into a comprehensive financial ecosystem supporting businesses, households and the country's economic development.

Bank Negara Malaysia governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said Islamic finance accounted for 48 per cent of Malaysia's total financial assets, with its share expected to surpass 50 per cent within the next few years.

"The industry contributed RM160 billion in issuance of sukuk to fund the real economic sector in 2025. Islamic banks' business financing grew by 9.7 per cent, supporting businesses across various economic sectors, while MSME microfinancing growth stood at 13.3 per cent," he told Bernama.

The governor also noted that Malaysia's position as the world's most developed Islamic finance market for the 14th consecutive year, as recognised in the Islamic Finance Development Report (IFDI) 2026, reflects four decades of sustained efforts in developing a comprehensive and progressive Islamic financial ecosystem.
Going forward, Bank Negara will continue working with the industry and its partners to advance innovation with purpose, digitalisation and sustainable finance.
The History of Malaysia's Islamic Finance Industry

Malaysia's Islamic finance industry has undergone several phases of development since the establishment of its first Islamic bank, Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd (BIMB), incorporated in March 1983 and officially commencing operations on July 1, 1983.

Recounting the industry's evolution with enthusiasm, Abdul Rasheed outlined four key phases in Islamic finance development, which are foundation-building from 1983 to 2000, mainstreaming from 2001 to 2010, diversification and innovation from 2011 to 2021 and advancing value-based finance from 2022 until today.

He explained that the introduction of Islamic banking windows enabled conventional banks to offer Shariah-compliant financial services, while the development of the Islamic interbank money market also provided the infrastructure needed to support the industry's growth.
"These developments laid the foundation for Islamic banking to grow from a niche offering into a mainstream component of Malaysia's financial system," he said.

The country also remains a key player in Asean's Islamic finance market, with Malaysian institutions accounting for about 82 per cent of the region's Islamic banking assets and 91 per cent of its takaful business.
Islamic Finance Offers Broader Financing Solutions through Risk-Sharing

Abdul Rasheed said Islamic finance offers a broader range of financing solutions through diverse contracts, including profit-sharing and partnership arrangements, which allow for greater risk-sharing.

He said both conventional and Islamic finance serve a similar economic objective of mobilising savings and financing businesses, but Islamic finance is distinguished by Shariah principles that require financing to support real economic activities and create value for borrowers, shareholders and the wider economy.

"Islamic finance also emphasises fairness, transparency, trust and good governance, while its diverse contractual structures enable financial institutions to offer solutions beyond conventional lending, including investment accounts with different risk-return profiles," he said.
The governor said takaful also has a distinct structure, with a clear separation between the operator and participants, who collectively own the risk fund.
Wonders of Social Finance
Abdul Rasheed said zakat and waqf could be combined with commercial financing to help recipients build sustainable livelihoods rather than remain dependent on financial assistance.
This approach aligns with value-based intermediation (VBI), which seeks to ensure that Islamic financial institutions generate positive outcomes for people and society alongside financial returns.

"Malaysia introduced the iTEKAD initiative during the Covid-19 pandemic to further advance social financing to support low-income microentrepreneurs and underserved communities. The programme has expanded from 57 participants in 2020 to about 16,000 participants today.

"The participating entrepreneurs recorded a 92 per cent increase in monthly sales and created more than 2,400 jobs. Some participants had also progressed from being zakat recipients to zakat contributors as their incomes improved, while digital-enabled transactions, including QR payment connectivity, facilitated them to reach wider markets, including overseas buyers," he said.

The initiative has since expanded to include employment support and access to the halal ecosystem through the new "Dapur iTEKAD KITA", a shared central kitchen that provides entrepreneurs with access to halal-certified, commercial-grade facilities to support business growth and market expansion.

This initiative builds on the experience of a programme launched in Penang at the Penang Times Square complex, involving 40 selected microentrepreneurs, most of whom originally started their businesses from home.
Abdul Rasheed said the second central kitchen is expected to be established in Seberang Perai, Penang, by mid-2027, as part of efforts to replicate the initiative nationwide.
Greening Halal Business to Help MSMEs Access Global Markets

For halal businesses, Abdul Rasheed said adopting sustainable practices is increasingly important as the global marketplace places greater emphasis on environmental standards and supply-chain requirements.

He said the Greening Halal Business (GHB) programme provides hands-on and practical support to halal businesses, particularly SMEs and medium-sized companies involved in the halal supply chain or halal-related services, to adopt sustainable practices and reduce carbon emissions.

He said adopting such practices would improve MSMEs' (micro, small and medium enterprises) ability to meet increasingly stringent environmental requirements in export markets, including Europe, while enhancing their capacity to supply multinational companies (MNCs).
"Islamic financial institutions could play a greater role in supporting this transition by providing appropriate financing alongside technical assistance and capacity-building support," he said.
Innovation with Purpose, Finance for Impact

The governor said the industry's future direction would be guided by the principle of "innovation with purpose, finance for impact", with the aim of generating better jobs, higher incomes, and a more sustainable, resilient economy.
"We want to build a nation where people live longer, healthier and financially secure," he said.
In addition, he said Islamic finance should embrace innovation that delivers tangible economic and social benefits, while ensuring financing reaches businesses and individuals who need it.
At the same time, he said innovation must deliver practical benefits, including improving access to financing for underserved communities, enhancing credit assessments and reducing transaction costs.
"Technology could help financial institutions assess borrowers who may lack conventional credit records by analysing their financial behaviour and repayment patterns," he said.

a9031c2f4bab67af: OCTOBER 25 — Brazil’s presidential election on October 25, 2026, is more than a contest between President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro. It is another important test of the direction of contemporary politics, where the political right has acquired increasing influence across several regions of the world.
For Asean, the implications deserve serious scrutiny.
Brazil may be geographically distant from Southeast Asia, but the ideological currents shaping its politics are not.
Nationalism, economic insecurity, political polarisation, hostility towards established institutions and dissatisfaction with traditional political parties are increasingly visible across continents.
The latest opinion polls demonstrate how closely divided Brazil has become.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Supporters of Brazil's right-wing Senator and presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro attend a campaign rally on the eve of the second round of the presidential election at the Barra da Tijuca neighbourhood of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil on October 24, 2026. — AFP pic
A CNT/MDA survey released on October 24 places Flávio Bolsonaro at 46.3 per cent against Lula’s 45 per cent.
The survey, conducted between October 21 and 23 among 2,032 respondents, has a margin of error of 2.2 percentage points.
The statistical difference is therefore insufficient to establish a clear leader.
Lula has also narrowed the gap in recent surveys, suggesting that Brazil’s electorate remains deeply contested rather than decisively committed to either political direction.
Yet the broader significance is unmistakable.
The Bolsonaro political movement has remained electorally substantial despite the controversies surrounding Jair Bolsonaro’s presidency and his subsequent conviction over an attempted coup.
Its continued appeal raises an important question about the durability of right-wing populism in democratic societies.
The Brazilian experience suggests that political movements can survive the departure of their founders when their underlying constituencies remain dissatisfied with existing institutions.
This phenomenon is hardly confined to Latin America.
Across Europe, right-wing parties have drawn support from anxieties over immigration, national identity, economic stagnation and the perceived failures of political elites.
In the United States, President Donald Trump has demonstrated how nationalism and economic grievances can be combined into an enduring political movement.
Brazil belongs within this larger transformation, although each country’s political circumstances remain distinct.
The danger for Asean is not that Southeast Asian societies will mechanically reproduce Brazil’s political trajectory.
Rather, political developments elsewhere can strengthen narratives that already exist within the region.
When political movements abroad emphasise national identity, cultural insecurity and resentment towards established elites, similar arguments may acquire greater visibility in Southeast Asia.
Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and the Philippines have different political systems and histories.
Nevertheless, all must contend with the relationship between economic expectations, identity politics and democratic accountability.
In Malaysia, the interaction between ethnicity, religion and political competition is particularly important.
The country’s political landscape has long been shaped by negotiations among Malay-Muslim political interests, minority communities, regional identities and competing visions of national development.
A more polarised international political environment could complicate these negotiations.
Political actors may increasingly frame economic dissatisfaction through questions of identity rather than public policy.
Such tendencies can narrow the space for compromise, especially in a plural society where constitutional arrangements depend upon sustained intercommunal understanding.
Indonesia faces a different challenge.
As the world’s largest Muslim-majority democracy, Indonesia must reconcile its democratic institutions with nationalism, religious mobilisation and the demands of economic transformation.
Its experience demonstrates that nationalism is not inherently incompatible with democratic pluralism.
Much depends upon whether political leaders employ national identity to strengthen inclusive institutions or to marginalise competing voices.
Thailand, meanwhile, continues to confront tensions between conservative institutions, reformist movements and competing understandings of political legitimacy.
The Philippines has its own experience of personality-driven politics, where family networks, popular mobilisation and law-and-order narratives have shaped electoral competition.
None of these countries can be reduced to a Brazilian political template.
Nevertheless, developments in Brazil provide another opportunity to examine how democratic competition changes when ideological polarisation becomes deeply embedded.
There is also a significant geopolitical dimension.
Brazil is a founding member of BRICS, a grouping that has become increasingly relevant to debates over multipolarity, international economic governance and the distribution of global influence.
Malaysia and Indonesia have sought closer engagement with BRICS as part of their wider diplomatic diversification.
Under Lula, Brazil has emphasised South-South cooperation, multilateral diplomacy and greater representation for developing economies.
A Bolsonaro administration could adopt different priorities, particularly regarding relations with Washington, environmental governance and the political orientation of BRICS.
These possibilities should not be confused with established policy decisions.
They would depend upon the composition of any new administration, domestic institutional constraints and Brazil’s economic interests.
Even so, Asean cannot assume that the strategic preferences of major emerging economies will remain unchanged after elections.
Brazil’s political contest also has implications for climate diplomacy.
The Amazon rainforest remains crucial to global biodiversity and climate stability.
Environmental policy has consequently become one of the important dividing lines between Lula and the Bolsonaro political movement.
Lula’s administration has pursued reductions in Amazon deforestation, while environmental campaigners have expressed concern over the implications of a possible return to Bolsonaro-family leadership.
For Southeast Asia, where deforestation, haze, biodiversity loss and extreme weather already present serious challenges, the international direction of climate policy is consequential.
A weakening of global environmental cooperation could make regional sustainability objectives more difficult to achieve.
Yet Asean must also recognise that right-wing politics is not a uniform phenomenon.
Conservative parties may support constitutional government, market reform and national sovereignty without embracing exclusionary nationalism or weakening democratic institutions.
The distinction between democratic conservatism and illiberal populism therefore matters.
Treating all right-wing movements as identical would obscure the very political developments that Asean needs to understand.
Similarly, Lula’s political difficulties cannot be explained exclusively through the ideological appeal of his opponents.

Concerns over living costs, crime, economic opportunity and dissatisfaction with government performance are legitimate electoral issues. The Associated Press has identified these concerns as central to the Brazilian campaign.
Governments that fail to address such grievances may find that voters increasingly turn towards alternative political movements.
The deeper lesson for Asean is therefore institutional rather than partisan.

Democratic resilience depends upon governments delivering economic security, maintaining public confidence, respecting constitutional procedures and preserving the legitimacy of political competition.
Asean’s own principles of consensus, inclusiveness and respect for diversity remain relevant, but they must be supported by practical governance.
Regional stability cannot rest exclusively upon diplomatic declarations while domestic societies experience rising economic anxiety and declining confidence in political institutions.
Brazil’s election should also remind Asean that multipolarity does not necessarily produce ideological moderation.
A world containing several centres of power may simultaneously experience sharper nationalism, more contested international institutions and greater competition over political values.
This is especially significant for Asean’s pursuit of centrality.
Asean cannot exercise even its circumscribed power effectively if its member states become increasingly divided by domestic ideological conflicts or external political alignments.
The Asean Outlook on the Indo-Pacific offers a framework for cooperation, inclusiveness and open regionalism.
Its credibility will depend upon whether member states continue to uphold these principles amid intensifying global competition.
Brazil’s presidential runoff has not yet produced a final verdict. Its close polling figures underscore the uncertainty of the contest.
Regardless of the outcome, the strength of competing political movements illustrates the depth of Brazil’s political divisions.
For Asean, the central concern is not simply whether Brazil moves further right or remains under Lula.
It is whether the broader international environment becomes increasingly polarised, leaving less room for compromise, pluralism and effective multilateral cooperation.
A global movement towards more confrontational politics would not stop at the geographical boundaries of Southeast Asia.
Asean must therefore understand the changing ideological landscape without assuming that political developments abroad will inevitably determine its own future.
Brazil’s election is a reminder that economic security, institutional legitimacy and social cohesion are essential foundations of political stability.
The challenge for Asean is to preserve these foundations while the international political landscape continues to change.
For a region built upon diversity, accommodation and diplomatic flexibility, that challenge is already substantial.
And it will not disappear when Brazil finishes counting its votes.
* Phar Kim Beng, PhD, is Professor of Asean Studies at the International Islamic University of Malaysia and Director of the Institute of International and Asean Studies (IINTAS).

14ed63655506e802: KUALA TERENGGANU, Oct 25 — The Sessions Court here today discharged and acquitted a retired Rubber Industry Smallholders Development Authority (Risda) employee of six charges of misappropriating RM15,350 in association funds about 10 years ago.
Judge Azman Mustapha made the decision after finding that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case against Mohd Amran Ghazali, 61, at the close of the defence case.

“I have considered the case against the accused and found that the money used by the accused was for Risda state (association) programmes, and this is consistent with the testimony of the 7th prosecution witness,” Azman said in his judgment.
The court also ordered the return of the accused’s earlier bail of RM6,000.
In 2021, Mohd Amran, then serving as an administrative assistant at the Terengganu Risda Office, was charged with six counts of misappropriating RM15,350 between 2016 and 2017.

Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) deputy public prosecutor Nur Amalina Najwa Mohd Ali appeared for the prosecution, while Mohd Amran was represented by lawyer Muhammad Abdul Rahman Ab Razak. — Bernama
89fb5bdc0906bd2a: PHNOM PENH: Cambodia is prioritising small-scale manufacturing industries and high-impact agriculture to drive its next phase of growth, as an economic slowdown and mounting headwinds pose challenges.

Weak tourism, rising fuel costs and climate risks are undermining growth, while rising incomes and surging domestic demand for food are putting pressure on the farm sector, forcing the government to rethink its strategies.

"Cambodia must transform from a producer of raw agricultural commodities into a hub for quality, safe and technologically advanced agri-food processing," Industry, Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Hem Vanndy said at the "Cambodia Agriculture Forum and Exhibition 2026" on Saturday.
He said agricultural exports remained dominated by raw or semi-processed products, generating limited added value and leaving producers exposed to international price fluctuations.

Multiple factors – including a decline in tourism revenue, high diesel and petrol prices, geopolitical tensions, the closure of the Cambodia-Thailand border following a territorial dispute, and reduced household spending – are stifling this year's growth prospects.
The World Bank in October downscaled Cambodia's economic growth to 3.5 per cent for 2026 from an earlier forecast of 3.9 per cent in April.
Last week, Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet launched the "National Strategy for MSME Development 2026-2030" to steer the sector that remains a backbone of the economy.

"The government is prioritising the development of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) through improved business conditions, improved productivity, technology adoption, better access to finance and skills development as Cambodia prepares to graduate from least developed country (LDC) status by the end of 2029," Hun Manet said last Thursday, as reported by state media Agence Kampuchea Presse.
The MSME sector contributes about 63 per cent of the country's gross domestic product (GDP), providing over 70 per cent of non-agricultural jobs.
About 750,000 MSMEs employ nearly three million workers, including 1.8 million women, according to the 2022 Economic Census, reported the state media.

"Indeed, MSMEs are the backbone of the national economy and key partners of the government in creating jobs, generating household income, promoting domestic production and strengthening economic resilience," he said.
The prime minister stated that the sector still faces challenges such as limited capital, technical capacity, market access, competition, high production costs, and bureaucratic procedures.
The agriculture sector is equally important, contributing about 16 per cent of GDP and employing over three million workers.

When Cambodia graduates from least developed country (LDC) status in 2029, it could lose some preferential trade benefits. This could expose key exports, including garments, rice and other agricultural products, to higher tariffs and stricter rules of origin in major markets.

The government is strengthening infrastructure, promoting advanced drying, cold-storage and packaging technologies, and prioritising the development of agro-industrial clusters to further propel these sectors.
There is also a focus on deploying modern farming technologies, including smart tractors and drones for fertiliser application.
Around 400 exhibitors are participating in the exhibition, which runs from Oct 23 to 25 at the Diamond Island Convention and Exhibition Centre in Phnom Penh.
a65c69cdf927ec7a: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 25 — The body of a man buried in a landslide at a two-storey semi-detached house in Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong, here, was recovered by firefighters at 11.20am today.

413e7c660a1e0b67: KUALA TERENGGANU: A 22-year-old man has been acquitted and discharged on three charges of rape and sexual assault involving a 12-year-old girl by the Sessions Court.

9843520f282045c5: KOTA KINABALU: The actions of a group of Malaysians believed to be from Sabah and Sarawak who insulted the Jalur Gemilang overseas risk tarnishing the reputation of Malaysians studying and working there.

The group claimed the event outside the Victorian Parliament House in Melbourne was significant in pressing for greater international attention to historical issues, the rights of the people, and the political future of Sabah and Sarawak.

Mustapha also encouraged the public to lodge official complaints with the police over the group's actions so that social media content showing the national flag upside down could be investigated under the relevant laws.
He said the situation today was different from more than 20 years ago, when efforts to push for the implementation of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) were considered a sensitive issue.

"More than 20 years ago, the MA63 struggle was considered sensitive, with some people detained by the authorities and facing legal action. Today, the rights of Sabah and Sarawak can be discussed openly and have even become a key agenda of the Madani government," he said.

"The people can judge for themselves the results achieved through negotiations and action compared with provocations such as these," he said.

c087f2814c56d7ad: KUALA LUMPUR: Pakatan Harapan needs more than 30 per cent of the Malay vote to win most of the seats it contests in the Melaka election.
Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari said Malay voter support is a key deciding factor, as many constituencies in the state have mixed voter demographics that will see tight contests.
He said PH also faces the challenge of identity politics, which could sway voting patterns, particularly in marginal seats.
"PH needs to secure more than 30 per cent of the Malay vote, and if we achieve that, we have a chance to win most seats.

"If we get around 20 per cent, we may only be able to add a few seats. However, if we fail to reach 20 per cent, PH risks losing some of the seats we currently hold," he said in an interview with Mingguan Malaysia.

Adly, who is also deputy defence minister, said PH has not discussed naming a poster boy for the state election, as the coalition's strategy focuses on ensuring every candidate works to win their respective state assembly seat.
He said having a poster boy provides no advantage if the candidate fails to win or defend the contested seat.
"Decisions regarding a poster boy have not been discussed at the state level or within the PH secretariat. I am also unsure whether the matter has been deliberated in the Presidential Council.
"In previous elections, a poster boy was usually only discussed in the Presidential Council, and only if raised. For now, there is no discussion on a poster boy.
"Everyone has their own views, and each party actually has its own poster boy. I think all parties have one, except for DAP, which I have not heard of having a poster boy," he said.
Adly said PH did not feature a poster boy during the Johor state election, while the then menteri besar served as the primary face of the coalition in the Negri Sembilan state election.
"The most important thing in facing an election is winning seats. Sometimes, as seen in the previous Melaka election, one poster boy was featured, but another individual was ultimately chosen.

"In Negri Sembilan, BN also had no official poster boy, though they had an individual seen as one. Yet in the end, someone else was chosen, as mentioned by the Umno president: what was ordered was different from what was received," he said.
Commenting on the challenge posed by Bersama, Adly said PH does not underestimate the party's ability to draw support, particularly among new voters.
He said several issues raised by Bersama align with PH's platform, potentially influencing PH supporters if internal discord arises.
"Looking at Johor, what matters most is that we remain united. If PH is divided, some PH voters will go to Bersama.
"Bersama mostly seeks votes among new voters. The number of new voters is relatively high, and we are competing for their support.
"We know Bersama's capabilities. The party is relatively new, but we have never viewed Bersama as a minor party," he said.
Adly said past election experience showed that even a single vote could determine victory, particularly in closely contested seats.
"Bersama may not win, but they can disrupt any contesting party's chances of victory.

"If we look at Pengkalan Batu in the last election, independent candidate Datuk Norhizam Hassan Baktee secured more than 1,000 votes, leading to a BN victory. That seat should have been a safe seat for PH. With Bersama, we must consider that factor," he said.

In the 2021 Melaka state election, Norhizam secured 1,218 votes in Pengkalan Batu, while BN candidate Datuk Kalsom Noordin won with a 131-vote majority after securing 4,839 votes against the PH candidate's 4,708 votes.
In the same election, BN won 21 of the 28 state seats, while PH won five and Perikatan Nasional took two.

Bersama has declared its intention to contest solo in the Melaka state election and announced candidates for several seats targeted by PH, including Pengkalan Batu, Ayer Keroh, Bukit Katil, Kesidang, and Kota Laksamana.
The Election Commission has set nomination day for the Melaka state election on Oct 31, with polling on Nov 14, 2026.

5671014178ff4b49: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia must learn from Thailand and Indonesia to improve their competitiveness at the next Asian Para Games after finishing 12th overall at the Aichi-Nagoya edition with six golds, eight silvers and 13 bronzes.
Paralympic Council of Malaysia (PCM) president Datuk Seri Megat D Shahriman Zaharudin said the two Southeast Asian nations had finished in the top 10, setting a benchmark for Malaysia.
"We achieved our six-gold target. Although our contingent was small, we still managed to meet the target and record an outstanding achievement.

"I believe Malaysia must match Thailand and Indonesia, who finished in the top 10. Perhaps their larger contingents helped them achieve those positions. We also need to learn from their formula and strategies," he said during a press conference on the Malaysian contingent's performance at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games, which concluded on Saturday after seven days of competition.
China topped the medal table with 207 golds, 117 silvers and 111 bronzes, followed by Japan (64-60-62) and Uzbekistan (45-49-51).
Thailand (19-40-66) and Indonesia (15-21-37) finished seventh and eighth respectively.
Malaysia sent 68 athletes to compete in 94 events across 10 of the 18 sports contested, making it the country's smallest contingent at the Asian Para Games.
Malaysia's six gold medals came from five sports, with two won in para athletics.
Wong Kar Gee won the men's long jump T12 (visual impairments), while Abdul Latif Romly topped the men's long jump T20 (intellectual impairments).
The para badminton pair of Cheah Liek Hou and Faris Azri won the men's doubles SU5 title, while para track cyclist Zuhairie Ahmad Tarmizi claimed gold in the men's 1,000m time trial C4-C5.
The other two gold medals came from Bonnie Bunyau Gustin in the men's under-72kg powerlifting event and swimmer Nur Syaiful Zulkafli in the men's100m breaststroke SB4.
Meanwhile, National Sports Council (NSC) director-general Arrifin Ghani said the athletes' overall performance had improved compared with the Hangzhou 2022 edition.

"We are grateful that we managed to meet our gold medal target. Overall, the athletes performed well and, in percentage terms, this edition's achievement was better than in Hangzhou four years ago," he said.

Arrifin said the NSC would work with the PCM and the National Sports Institute (NSI) to strengthen programmes and assess which sports had the potential to deliver more medals at next year's Asean Para Games on home soil and the 2028 Los Angeles Paralympics. - BERNAMA

25fbf32ae6180f15: SINGAPORE, Oct 25 — The republic’s gas importers will use all available measures to protect their contractual rights, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said today after Indonesia's decision to curb pipeline gas exports.

Addressing the People's Action Party (PAP) conference, Wong noted that while piped natural gas remains central to power generation, investments in liquefied natural gas (LNG) import terminals have diversified Singapore's supply chains against single-source vulnerabilities. The Straits Times reported.
“We expect all parties to honour their commitments, and Singapore’s gas importer will take the necessary steps to protect its rights and interests under these contracts,” Wong said.

His remarks follow an announcement by Indonesia's upstream regulator, SKK Migas, reducing piped gas exports to Singapore by 31 billion British thermal units per day (BBTUD) from Oct 24 under President Prabowo Subianto's domestic energy drive.

Singapore's Energy Market Authority (EMA) clarified that local importers face a smaller reduction of 17 BBTUD over 18 days, representing under 2 per cent of national daily demand exceeding 1,000 BBTUD.

Looking ahead, Wong said Singapore requires “cleaner sources of power to provide reliable electricity around the clock”, confirming ongoing feasibility studies into nuclear energy despite safety and waste concerns in a dense city-state.

“We take the concerns very seriously. Safety must come first. But we should not rule out an option simply because it is difficult or controversial,” he said. Singapore will undergo an International Atomic Energy Agency assessment in 2027 to gauge deployment readiness.
Wong added that cross-border challenges, including transboundary haze and online scams, demand regional cooperation alongside domestic vigilance.
“We are doing everything we can within our power to protect Singaporeans, strengthen our own response and work with our partners to tackle these problems at source.”

82fa11623bb3a62f: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 25 — A man was confirmed dead after being buried in a landslide that affected a house in Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong here today.

Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations John Sagun Francis said it received an emergency call at 8.36am and a team from the Paya Terubong Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to the scene.

“Upon arrival, we found that the landslide had affected the back section of a house, and initial reports indicated that three people, believed to be occupants of the house, were involved in the incident.

“Two of them managed to save themselves, while the third was believed to be trapped and buried, before being confirmed dead at 9.10am by Health Ministry personnel at the scene,” he said in a statement today.
He said that as of 9.45am, firefighters were working to extricate the victim from under the rubble.

The operation involved seven firefighters, including a supervisor, as well as a Light Fire Rescue Tender (LFRT) and an Emergency Medical Rescue Service (EMRS) unit, with assistance from the police. — Bernama
6b23c9c154729a49: PHILLIP ISLAND, Oct 25 — Marc Marquez was denied the chance Sunday to stretch his world championship lead over injured Jorge Martin with the last Australian MotoGP at Phillip Island cancelled due to treacherous conditions.
Organisers pulled the plug despite a sell-out crowd with persistent rain and poor visibility making racing unsafe. The Moto3 and Moto2 races were also cancelled. — AFP
1c35f93a62276558: KUCHING: The National Population and Family Development Board (LPPKN) has allocated RM9 million for mammogram screening subsidies expected to benefit nearly 40,000 women nationwide next year.
Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the allocation is part of government efforts to encourage more women to undergo early breast cancer screening.
She said the government hopes more women will utilise the initiative for early detection.
"For next year, 38,000 women (nationwide) will benefit from this subsidy, with an estimated 9,000 of them in Sarawak," she said.
She said this after officiating the Sarawak State-Level Breast Cancer Awareness Month 2026 celebrations at Padang Merdeka here today.
Nancy said women are encouraged to register early to secure screening slots through the available facilities.
"LPPKN introduced the Mammogram Subsidy Programme in 2007 as a government initiative to widen access to early breast cancer screening.
"As of Sept 30, the programme has benefited 598,919 women nationwide.
"In Sarawak alone, 90,075 women benefited and underwent screening, with 88 detected positive for cancer," she said.
She said mammogram screening facilities in Sarawak are available at several hospitals across the state, including in Kuching, Sibu, and Miri.
"This step is vital to ensure women have easier access to screening, especially in efforts to detect breast cancer early," she said.
She said early screening is critical as breast cancer remains among the most common cancers affecting women in Malaysia.
Nancy said women should not wait until they reach 40 to undergo screening, but instead seek early checks.
She said women aged 18 and above should be encouraged to undergo screening, while those in high-risk categories must pay particular attention to checks once they reach 40.

84f611b3590f2586: GEORGE TOWN: A stop-work order has been issued following a landslide in Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong, with occupants of five houses advised to evacuate as a precaution.
Penang Island City Council (MBPP) mayor Datuk A. Rajendran said the affected project involves the construction of a road and apartments, which has been ongoing for more than a year.
He said the Land Office will coordinate arrangements for residents who need to be relocated.
"For now, a stop-work order has been issued against the development project near the landslide site.
"Also, we have advised the other residents to leave. The Land Office will handle the arrangements," he said when met at the scene.
Asked whether MBPP had been monitoring ground movement behind the affected area, Rajendran said the project's consultants would be responsible for conducting the necessary assessments.
He declined to comment further, saying investigations would be carried out to determine the circumstances surrounding the incident.
Earlier today, a man was killed after a landslide struck the rear of his house in Taman Seri Rambai.
731c1175b95131ce: COLOMBO: Sri Lanka is determined to accelerate its transition to renewable energy spurred by soaring oil prices, but faces major constraints, its energy minister told AFP.
"There are some wake-up calls... pushing us to move more to renewable energy," Anura Karunathilaka said.
"If we can get as much as possible from renewable energy, that would be our policy in the next few years."
The island nation, which imports all its oil and gas needs, has been hit hard since the US and Israel launched their war on Iran, which in turn choked off the strategically critical Strait of Hormuz.

Sharp increases in fuel, gas and electricity prices, rationing and inflation at its highest in three years have dealt a painful blow to an economy only just recovering from its worst-ever crisis in 2022.
The state and the public have paid a heavy price.
The energy ministry says the government has at times spent up to 30 percent of its foreign exchange reserves in a single month to pay for fossil fuel imports.
Sri Lanka's energy transition targets were set before the war.
By 2030, the country aims to generate 70% of its electricity from renewable sources, up from around 60% currently, including about 40% from hydropower.
Promise to the people
"We will probably have to go beyond 70%," Karunathilaka said.
But the transition is proving more complicated than expected.
Some communities oppose wind turbines.

The island has enormous potential for wind power -- estimated at 30 gigawatts-- but anger is growing on the northwestern Mannar peninsula, where residents blame turbines operating since 2020 for causing floods, driving fish away and threatening migratory birds.
The minister said he had listened to their concerns.
"We have promised the people of Mannar... that only projects already approved or under construction will go ahead," he said, adding that future wind farms would be built elsewhere.
Another obstacle is technical.
"The problem is the constraint in the transmission lines, availability and also control of the grid, as well as fluctuations in supply and demand," Karunathilaka said.
"From next year onwards, we have planned to enhance our transmission capacity, adding five major transmission network lines."
But that will not be enough.

The success of solar power, particularly the installation of photovoltaic panels on homes and businesses, has created sharp fluctuations in electricity supply, which often exceeds demand during daylight hours.
Pricing changes
This month a six-hour blackout struck across the island after the national grid tripped, possibly because solar power generation exceeded consumption.

"Sometimes we have to curtail certain solar power plants to maintain the stability of the system. That is why some people have the perception that the government is not encouraging solar power," Karunathilaka said. "But that is not true."
By 2029, the government hopes to increase its solar power generation capacity to nearly 4,400 megawatts, a 388% jump from 2024, he said.
However, he added that the government would have to change how solar electricity was priced.

Under the existing system, private producers can feed electricity into the grid during the day, when generation is at its peak and demand is low, then draw back the same amount for free at night, when electricity is more expensive.
The arrangement is financially unsustainable for a fragile economy, the minister said.

"The additional cost is borne by the state," he said. "We think it is unfair to pass that burden on to the general public, so we will propose a new financial model that is fair to both solar producers and consumers."
The government also plans to expand electricity storage using batteries, Karunathilaka said.
"The system, investment and infrastructure are not yet ready to completely replace coal and naphtha," he warned.
"But... in 10 to 15 years, we will also be reducing naphtha and coal, and we will be able to achieve 90-95 percent renewable energy."
4bbdf89c29627cb3: LONDON: Britain's government set out around £600 million (US$800 million) of funding on Saturday largely geared towards defending against health and security threats from artificial intelligence (AI).

The biggest chunk of funding will go to a new biosecurity initiative, including £100 million for a laboratory using AI to detect biological threats and £65 million to develop countermeasures against pathogens.

AI minister Kanishka Narayan said the aim was for the AI Biosecurity Lab to become a major global institution "bringing together world-leading scientific expertise to protect people from emerging biological threats."
Tech companies OpenAI and Anthropic will offer up to £200 million of model credits to the biosecurity initiative.
Google DeepMind and London-based AI life sciences startup Basecamp Research will offer other assistance.
Britain's government will give its existing AI Security Institute an extra £120 million.

£130 million will go towards new projects to improve cyber defences for critical infrastructure and the wider economy, known as the National Cyber Shield and the National Exposure and Real-Time Vulnerability Centre.
£60 million will go towards a fund that will invest in British companies using AI to advance robotics, autonomous systems and manufacturing.
£60 million will be used for AI research and procurement contracts
An extra £23 million will go to research on the economic impact of AI.
£18 million will go to a new chip design academy.
£15 million will fund a prize for AI solutions to public policy problems, initially focused on healthcare.
£30 million will go to regional mayors to support local AI work.
Britain's National Cyber Security Centre will receive an unspecified sum to expand in Manchester.
Anthropic alone racked up more than US$12 billion in operating expenses last year.
ff5f69131dae0df8: PETALING JAYA: Pakatan Harapan's objective in the Melaka polls is to add to the five seats it previously held in the state assembly, rather than win the state election, says state chairman Adly Zahari.
Adly said PH acknowledged it would be a mammoth task to regain control of the Melaka government, Utusan Malaysia reported.
"That's why our focus in Melaka is to add to our number of seats, not to regain power in the state," said the Melaka PH chief.
In the 2021 Melaka polls, BN won 21 seats, while PH garnered five and Perikatan Nasional two.
Adly said there was always the possibility that the state election would result in a hung state assembly, forcing the formation of a coalition government, similar to the federal administration.
The Amanah vice-president said Umno appeared aware of this fact, judging by its decision to form an electoral pact with PAS for the state polls.
The two-term Bukit Katil assemblyman said it was therefore crucial for PH to win about 30% of the Malay vote to emerge victorious in several key battlegrounds.
"If we only garner 20% of Malay votes, we may only be able to add a few seats.
"However, if we fail to even reach 20%, we risk losing some of the seats we won previously," said Adly, who acknowledged that his Bukit Katil seat was also "at risk".
Adly is seeking a third term as assemblyman for Bukit Katil, a mixed seat where 65% of the electorate are Malays, followed by Chinese (29.7%) and Indians (4.26%).
He first won the seat with a 3,159-vote majority in 2018 before retaining it for a second term in 2021, albeit with a slimmer majority of 1,057 votes.
Adly, a former Melaka chief minister, also said there was no need for PH to name a poster boy for the state polls, adding that the coalition has never discussed the matter.
He said PH's strategy this time around is for each candidate to fully focus on their respective constituencies.
"It's no use having a poster boy who cannot win or defend his seat," he said.
Adly served as chief minister from 2018 to 2020, when he was ousted following the collapse of the PH-led administration at the state and federal levels.
1df6ef1889c73fca: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 25 — The water supply disruption in Tawau was raised at the Sabah Cabinet meeting last Wednesday to ensure immediate action is taken to help affected residents.

Sabah Youth Development, Sports Advancement and Creative Economy Minister Datuk Nizam Abu Bakar Titingan, who raised the matter, said dry weather and a prolonged lack of rain have affected raw water sources, disrupting treatment operations and distribution since last week.
“I raised this problem at the Cabinet meeting because I understand the difficulties faced by affected residents.
“Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor has also directed the Sabah Works and Utilities Ministry to have the Tawau Water Department (JANS) take proactive action.

“This includes intensifying water deliveries by tanker lorries to affected areas. Sabah Works and Utilities Minister Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam has assured that the issue is being monitored and capacity mobilised to help affected residents,” he said in a statement here today.
Nizam said the Tawau Water Department’s latest data showed that operations at the Utara Water Treatment Plant remain affected due to raw water quality problems from Sungai Tawau.
“Although there has been rain, the rainfall in the catchment area is still insufficient to significantly raise the river level and allow water treatment operations to recover fully.
He said water deliveries will continue according to current operational capacity, with better coordination to ensure affected areas receive due attention.
Nizam said the water supply problem cannot be taken lightly as it involves the people’s basic needs and affects households on a daily basis.
“I will be in touch with the ministry and JANS to get the latest developments on the situation and ensure the needs of affected residents continue to be addressed,” he said. — Bernama
6b990993012bdc76: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today congratulated the Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, on the Silver Jubilee of his reign.
In a Facebook post, Anwar also prayed that Sultan Sharafuddin would be blessed with good health and well-being to continue leading the people of Selangor with fairness and justice.

"Extending my highest congratulations on the occasion of the Silver Jubilee marking 25 years of the reign of His Royal Highness Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah Alhaj Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Shah Alhaj, Sultan and Yang Dipertuan of Selangor Darul Ehsan.

"May Allah Subhanahu Wa Ta'ala continue to grant His Royal Highness good health and lasting well-being, and may His Royal Highness remain steadfast in leading and protecting the people of Selangor with fairness and justice. Daulat Tuanku, Dirgahayu Tuanku," he said.
6b28439a6975a2d9: ISTANBUL: Bill Gates warned that artificial intelligence (AI) could trigger two decades of economic and social upheaval, disrupting jobs and life even if the technology is managed successfully, Anadolu Ajansi reported, citing Decoder podcast.

In an interview with the Decoder podcast posted Thursday, the Microsoft co-founder said the transition to an AI-driven economy would create winners and losers, potentially reshaping employment and raising questions about people's roles in society.

"My big concern is this 20-year transition period, where they'll have winners and losers and a lot of disruption," said Gates, 70, adding that society would have to navigate the upheaval before potentially entering an era of abundance.

He described the timeframe as an estimate rather than a firm prediction, acknowledging that the transition could be shorter or longer depending on technological advances and decisions about slowing development.

Gates said advances in AI and humanoid robotics could eventually allow machines to perform much of the physical labour carried out by humans, including building homes, growing food, and even performing surgery.

While the advances could reduce shortages of goods and services, he suggested societies might deliberately reserve certain activities for humans, including childcare, food preparation, arts, and sports.
The billionaire philanthropist also highlighted AI's potential benefits in healthcare and agriculture but warned that governments and society are not adequately prepared for its rapid development.
He urged stronger government oversight and technical safeguards against cyberattacks and biological threats, arguing that AI companies alone cannot be responsible for managing the risks.
Gates also warned that even under the most favourable circumstances, AI's development could bring one of the most tumultuous periods in human history.
"I hate being the bearer of concerning news on this, but it's even worse not to tell people that this is coming. We have choices as humans to make about how we shape it," he said.
3242fc23969c1bcc: KOTA BARU: A TikToker was fined RM4,500 by the magistrate's court after pleading guilty to insulting a woman's modesty by likening her to a prostitute last November.
Nur Hazwani Mustapha, 39, entered the plea before magistrate Vinoshen Raveentharan after the charge was read to her.
She was charged with insulting the modesty of Nur Faezah Sohaimi, 33, via WhatsApp on Nov 1, 2025.
The charge was framed under Section 509 of the Penal Code, which provides for up to five years' jail, a fine, or both upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Muhammad Baihaqi Mohd Saidi prosecuted, while lawyer Muhammad Husni Mubarak Ghazali represented Nur Hazwani.
In mitigation, Husni sought a minimum fine, saying Nur Hazwani was a single mother supporting four children aged 6 to 17 on her income as a laksa seller.
"This is also the accused's first offence," he said.
The court fined her RM4,500, which she paid.
df95c79bdfb35fb6: KUALA LUMPUR: S. Sivasangari has another Gold-level title under her belt, but the Malaysian is hungry for bigger prizes as she sets her sights on breaking into the world's top three.

The world No. 4 strengthened her credentials with a dominant victory at the Silicon Valley Open in Redwood City, California, on Saturday, beating Egypt's world No. 20 Farida Mohamed 11-7, 11-6, 11-8 in 31 minutes to claim her fourth Gold-level crown.
And Squash Racquets Association of Malaysia (SRAM) coaching director Andrew Cross believes Sivasangari is firmly on course to challenge the world's elite.
"She is definitely chasing for the top three ranking in the world," said Cross.
The 27-year-old's latest success adds to her Gold-level titles at the London Classic in 2024, and the Australian Open and Grasshopper Cup last season.
But Sivasangari is now determined to make the breakthrough at Platinum level, with the US Open in Philadelphia from Nov 1-7 her next opportunity.

She has already shown she can challenge the best, having reached the semi-finals of the Platinum-level Egyptian Open this month, where she narrowly lost to world No. 2 Hania El Hammamy in a deciding fifth game.
"And her next tournament will be the Platinum-level US Open," said Cross.

Sivasangari, who has trained under French coach Gregory Gaultier in Prague since last year, has continued to make progress against the leading players, including Egypt's top-ranked trio of world No. 1 Amina Orfi, Hania and world No. 3 Nour El Sherbini.
Her Silicon Valley victory was her third win in five meetings against Farida, 24, and took her career tally to 18 PSA titles from 28 final appearances since turning professional 15 years ago.
Sivasangari was pleased with how she handled the pressure of being the third seed in the draw.
"Definitely very happy with how I performed the whole week.
"There was a bit of pressure on me as the top two ranked players did not play in the tournament, so it was left to me to face the lower-ranked players.
"But, just happy with the way I handled it, stayed composed, and won the final in three games today," she told the PSA Squash Tour.
Having already earned her place at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics by retaining her Asian Games title last month, Sivasangari now has another challenge in her sights.

"Obviously, I have already won the Gold-level title at the beginning of this season. I told myself, I want to break through and go into the semi-finals of the Platinum events, which I have already done at the start of this season.
"So now I have to go one step higher and try to win a Platinum-level tournament."
fddc011941d5821b: GEORGE TOWN: A resident living near the Taman Seri Rambai landslide site heard a loud rumbling sound at 2am while he was sleeping.
Lim, in his 30s, said the noise sounded like rocks collapsing, prompting him to go outside to check.
"I was sleeping when I heard a loud sound, like rocks falling," he said when met.
Lim, who has lived in the area with his parents for more than 30 years, said he had long been concerned about landslide risks, particularly during heavy rain.
He said a previous landslide had occurred about 10 years ago behind a small temple in the area, after which repairs were carried out.
However, he said mud frequently spilled onto the road during heavy downpours, with workers called in to clear the affected stretch.
"The only action the developers take is to call workers to clean up the road. That's all," he said.
Lim said he had lodged complaints about his concerns but felt that action was unlikely unless an incident occurred.
He also questioned the approval of a proposed 47-storey development in the area, claiming that residents had opposed the project but it had proceeded.
He said residents were worried about the potential risks, especially during periods of heavy rainfall.
Lim added that the area's history of landslides made him question how the development had obtained approval.
It was reported that a man was killed after a landslide struck the rear of a house in Taman Seri Rambai, Paya Terubong, this morning.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said the department received an emergency call at 8.36am.

f0b19316178f39a7: KUALA LUMPUR: Actress Mia Sara Shauki accepts that comparisons to her father, renowned director Datuk Afdlin Shauki, are inevitable—especially now that she aims to follow in his footsteps as a film director.
The 27-year-old admitted she had always known this reality, and chooses to embrace it as she remains focused on her work.
"I can't change who my parents are. I've felt this since I was little, and as I grew older, I accepted that it's unavoidable.

"I accept it, and no matter what, I can always do my best. If I make a mistake or do something poorly, I have to face it myself, try to put it right, and hope I do not hurt anyone along the way," she told BH Online.
While acknowledging that her family name opens doors, Mia Sara believes those opportunities must be backed up by hard work, dedication, and a continuous desire to learn.
"If people say it is easier for me to get work because of my name, that is true, and I can accept it. With what I have now, I must do my best.
"If I cannot act well, I need to go and train. My father has always advised me to learn and practise before diving into any field.

"Whether it is the arts or even law, we genuinely have to study first and give it a try. If we try and do not succeed yet, it is completely fine because we can still learn from that experience," she said.
Unfazed by criticism of her acting, Mia Sara views external opinions as constructive feedback rather than taking them personally.
"Everyone has their own preferences. I cannot stop what people want to say. So, when I hear criticism, I can actually take it well because it can be used to learn further," she said.
Beyond honing her acting craft, Mia Sara is now taking steps towards her childhood dream of directing her own films.
Her passion for storytelling was sparked early on, as she often spent time on set with her father, drawing and brainstorming ideas together.
"Ever since I was little, I used to draw or tell stories with my father, and whenever he made a film, I would always visit the set.
"Right from the start, I knew that was his way of storytelling. There's a desire for me to do the same thing.

"After finishing filming for this drama, I plan to start directing a short film. The story is based on an original idea I had as a teenager," said the actress, who recently wrapped up shooting for the second season of the drama series Dorm 403.
Her upcoming short film explores her personal journey of discovering and drawing closer to Islam, a project she describes as a love letter to herself.
Through it, she hopes to highlight experiences that resonate with women across Malaysia, particularly the unique and deeply personal path each takes towards finding faith.
"This film is about opening your heart to Islam. I feel the story will resonate with many Malaysian women because we all face our own struggles.
"We may know how to be good women, but the journey to truly being touched by faith—whether that means choosing to wear the hijab or beginning to pray—is different for everyone.
"In a way, this film is a love letter to myself for discovering my faith," she said.

37b70fe45543980c: HEBRON: Israel said Sunday all land crossings with the West Bank will be closed on the day of next week's election, as it pledged a harder line on militancy after Palestinian gunmen killed two soldiers in the territory.

The announcement came a day after Israeli forces pushed into the occupied West Bank city of Hebron and displaced around 2,000 residents, with Defence Minister Israel Katz saying, "they will not be allowed to return... until we've finished dealing with all the Hamas issues in Hebron."
Hamas, while not claiming credit, hailed Friday's killings at a checkpoint near the Palestinian city, in which attackers shot dead two Israeli soldiers and wounded three more.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed to exact a heavy price for the attack just days before polls and said he was planning an operation on a scale not seen since Israel first occupied the West Bank in 1967.

The Israeli army said that, from Sunday, Palestinians would "not be permitted to enter Israeli communities in Judea and Samaria and the Jordan Valley for work", using terms many in Israel use to refer to the West Bank.

The army also said it would enforce "a ban on the entry and exit of Palestinian workers throughout Judea and Samaria and the Jordan Valley, including industrial zones, as well as the closure of all land crossings throughout Election Day" on Oct 27, it added.
Israel's longest serving prime minister Netanyahu is facing a tight race for a new term in Tuesday's polls, with his security-first reputation all but shattered by Hamas's Oct 7, 2023 attack.

The Palestinian Authority, the semi-autonomous body that governs parts of the West Bank in cooperation with Israel, called for international pressure on Israel to protect residents affected by the military operation.
The Israeli army said that over Friday and Saturday, it operated in 40 areas throughout the territory, with locals reporting that soldiers announced evacuations over loudspeakers late at night.
Israeli forces said they "apprehended approximately 40 suspects, including those affiliated with the Hamas and Islamic Jihad."
- 'PAINFUL PRICE' -
In the Hebron neighbourhood of Ein Deir Baha, nestled between two hills, vacated buildings were marked by X's and the streets were deserted, save a pair of Israeli military vehicles.
Israeli flags were draped on a house on the slope apparently taken over by troops.
Higazi Shawer al-Tamimi, 70, a shopkeeper who plays a leadership role in the neighbourhood, said he was awakened at 1am by soldiers and a senior officer who said he had to leave.
"I asked them how long the evacuation would last. They said: 'Until further notice.'"
He told AFP he had only a short time to pack, adding that for some residents, getting out of the neighbourhood was an ordeal.
"For example, my wife's mother, who is 90 years old and lives in the area, had to be carried out because she is ill," he said.

Right-wing Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, who also holds a position in the defence ministry overseeing civilian affairs in the West Bank, said he personally ordered "the immediate demolition of a row of illegal structures" following Friday's shooting.
"Anyone who messes with us will quickly understand that he will pay a painful price," he wrote on X.
To Tamimi, the West Bank operation is only happening because Netanyahu wants to win the election on "the blood of the Palestinian people."
He said people were not going anywhere. "I have lived through all the stages of the occupation, and I will die here."
But Tamimi's brother, Khaled Shawer al-Tamimi, 68, said he and his son left after the evacuation order rang out.
"The army was announcing through loudspeakers: 'Leave the area.' So we left."
He told AFP he was surprised to hear Friday's assailants came from the neighbourhood, which he described as middle-class and law-abiding.
"We have never seen or even heard a single gunshot being fired," he said from his son's sitting room as children flitted about.
The Israeli military said the operation would last several days, but Netanyahu suggested bigger action was coming.--AFP

9c76577211fbdbbb: PETALING JAYA: Dua pemimpin DAP mencabar MCA mengambil tindakan lebih drastik bagi menyuarakan rasa tidak puas hati mereka selepas meninggalkan majlis pengumuman calon Barisan Nasional (BN) bagi PRN Melaka semalam.
Ahli Parlimen Kampar, Chong Zhemin, mencabar MCA keluar daripada BN sepenuhnya, manakala Setiausaha Pemuda DAP, Lim Chun Weng, mencabar parti itu bertanding PRN Melaka menggunakan logo sendiri.

Chong berkata, episod itu memperlihatkan kedudukan MCA yang memalukan dalam BN, apabila kerusi yang sebelum ini ditandingi parti berkenaan diberikan kepada parti lain sebarang rundingan terlebih dahulu.
"Apakah bukti yang lebih jelas MCA tiada suara bermakna dalam BN?
"Umno menentukan siapa yang mendapat kerusi. MCA pula dijangka hadir, menerima keputusan itu dan memberikan tepukan.
"Persetujuan presiden MCA sendiri nampaknya dianggap perkara remeh yang boleh diketepikan," katanya dalam kenyataan.
Lim dalam kenyataan berasingan berkata, MCA sepatutnya bertanding PRN Melaka menggunakan logo sendiri. bukannya lambang BN demi menjaga maruah parti itu.
Jika tidak, katanya, tindakan pemimpin MCA meninggalkan majlis semalam tidak lebih daripada sekadar lakonan politik untuk meraih undi simpati.
"Jika MCA benar-benar merasakan BN tidak menghormatinya dan maruah MCA telah dipijak, maka jangan lagi bergantung kepada lambang dacing BN.
"Kalau benar ada maruah, gunakan logo MCA sendiri dan bertandinglah di kerusi tradisi MCA yang diserahkan kepada Perikatan Nasional.
Katanya, jika MCA akhirnya menerima keputusan BN dan tetap bertanding menggunakan lambang gabungan itu, kepimpinan parti berkenaan perlu berhenti menggambarkan diri sebagai mangsa.
Presiden MCA, Wee Ka Siong, mengetuai tindakan meninggalkan majlis BN di Melaka malam tadi ketika gabungan diterajui Umno itu mengumumkan calonnya bagi PRN 14 Nov ini.

ee81be4194ba9f3a: MELAKA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said a global investor plans to inject US$50 billion (RM204 billion) into the artificial intelligence (AI), new technology, and data centre sectors in Malaysia.
He said the investor conveyed the intention during a recent video conference, describing the proposed venture across Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia as one of the largest in the region.
